option_description: Whether the primary persistence layer (database, volume, or object store) applies at-rest encryption so storage-media compromise yields ciphertext rather than readable content.
security_impact: Satisfies "At-rest encryption enabled on all persisted stores" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when encrypted_at_rest is true alongside storage_encryption_enabled, tde_enabled and backups_encrypted. Confirms the protection mitigating cloud/local storage data theft (ATT&CK T1530/T1005, M1041; D3FEND D3-DENCR/D3-FE).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check that every RDS database instance reports storage encryption enabled (the primary managed-store exemplar).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: StorageEncrypted: true for every instance (secure); any false is an unencrypted store. Mirrors CIS AWS RDS.3.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark (Security Hub control mapping)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify a self-managed block device is encrypted by dumping its LUKS header.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A valid LUKS header with a Cipher line present (secure: the block device is encrypted); 'Device is not a valid LUKS device' means the volume is cleartext.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-111 Guide to Storage Encryption Technologies for End User Devices

option_description: Whether the underlying block/disk/object storage layer has volume- or bucket-level encryption enabled (e.g. EBS, S3 SSE, managed-disk encryption).
security_impact: Satisfies "At-rest encryption enabled on all persisted stores" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when storage_encryption_enabled is true together with encrypted_at_rest, tde_enabled and backups_encrypted. Protects against local/physical media theft (ATT&CK T1005, M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm EBS default encryption is on and that no volume is left unencrypted.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 get-ebs-encryption-by-default; aws ec2 describe-volumes --query 'Volumes[?Encrypted==`false`].VolumeId'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EbsEncryptionByDefault: true and an empty unencrypted-volume list (secure); any unencrypted volume is a gap. Mirrors CIS AWS EC2.7.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark (Security Hub control mapping)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For on-prem/self-managed volumes, verify the block device exposes a valid encryption header.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A valid LUKS header with a Cipher line present (secure); 'not a valid LUKS device' means the volume is cleartext.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-111 Guide to Storage Encryption Technologies for End User Devices

option_description: Whether the database engine applies Transparent Data Encryption so data files, transaction logs, and tempdb are encrypted at the storage layer.
security_impact: Satisfies "At-rest encryption enabled on all persisted stores" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when tde_enabled is true alongside encrypted_at_rest, storage_encryption_enabled and backups_encrypted. Ensures DB files/logs/backups are not written in cleartext (ATT&CK T1005, M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the DB instance reports storage encryption with a KMS key bound (RDS storage encryption also covers logs, automated backups, snapshots and read replicas).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: StorageEncrypted true with a KmsKeyId set (secure); false = cleartext DB storage.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark (Security Hub control mapping)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For a self-managed engine (SQL Server / Oracle / MySQL), confirm engine-level TDE is enabled on the database and its log files.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Engine reports TDE/encryption-state ENABLED for the database, log, and tempdb files; no datafile is written in cleartext.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether automated backups, snapshots, and exported copies inherit or enforce at-rest encryption — not just the live store.
security_impact: Satisfies "At-rest encryption enabled on all persisted stores" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when backups_encrypted is true with the other store flags. Closes the snapshot/backup exposure path where an unencrypted backup copy bypasses the primary store's protection (ATT&CK T1530, M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: List any self-owned EBS snapshots that are not encrypted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty list = all snapshots encrypted (secure); any returned SnapshotId is an unencrypted backup copy.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark (Security Hub control mapping)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the backup process to confirm backups/snapshots receive at-rest protection equivalent to primary data, with keys in a separate trust domain.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Review confirms backups/snapshots receive equivalent at-rest protection to primary data and their keys live in a separate trust domain.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-209 Security Guidelines for Storage Infrastructure

option_description: The at-rest cipher and key strength: strong = AES-256 (or AES-128 minimum) FIPS-approved algorithm; weak = legacy/short-key ciphers; none = unencrypted.
security_impact: Satisfies "FIPS-approved strong algorithm and key strength" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when at_rest_encryption_strength equals "strong" together with fips_validated_module true. Defeats weak/legacy-cipher cryptanalysis (DES/3DES/RC4) (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the cipher and key size from the encrypted volume's LUKS header.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: cipher: aes-xts-plain64 with a 512-bit keysize → AES-256 (XTS splits the key, so 512-bit keysize = AES-256) (secure); a non-AES or short-key cipher is weak.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-111 Guide to Storage Encryption Technologies for End User Devices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the algorithm is a FIPS-approved cipher implemented by a validated module, not legacy crypto.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Verify the crypto module backing the store appears on the NIST CMVP validated-modules list (FIPS 140-3). Requirement is not merely 'use AES-256' but 'use a CMVP-validated module'.
how_to_obtain.source: FIPS 140-3 / NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP)

option_description: Whether the encryption is performed by a FIPS 140-2/140-3 CMVP-validated cryptographic module rather than unvalidated or proprietary crypto.
security_impact: Satisfies "FIPS-approved strong algorithm and key strength" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when fips_validated_module is true alongside at_rest_encryption_strength == "strong". Assures the AES implementation is correctly validated, hardening against cryptanalytic recovery (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the module backing at-rest encryption appears on the NIST CMVP validated-modules list with an active certificate.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Verify the crypto module backing the store appears on the NIST CMVP validated-modules list (FIPS 140-3). Requirement is not merely 'use AES-256' but 'use a CMVP-validated module'.
how_to_obtain.source: FIPS 140-3 / NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Obtain the provider/vendor FIPS attestation (e.g. KMS HSM FIPS 140 level, or OS crypto module certificate number) and confirm it maps to the algorithms in use.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Provider attestation or CMVP certificate number naming the validated module and the approved algorithms (AES, SHA-2, HMAC) it implements.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether master/key-encryption keys live in a dedicated KMS or HSM in a separate trust domain from the data store, rather than in app config or alongside the ciphertext.
security_impact: Satisfies "Keys held in a dedicated KMS/HSM with envelope encryption" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when keys_managed_in_hsm_or_kms is true together with envelope_encryption_kek_dek_split. Prevents a single storage compromise from yielding both ciphertext and the key (ATT&CK T1552, M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: List KMS keys and confirm key material is managed in KMS/HSM rather than embedded with the data.
how_to_obtain.command: aws kms list-keys && aws kms describe-key --key-id <id> --query 'KeyMetadata.{mgr:KeyManager,origin:Origin,store:KeyStoreId}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key material managed in KMS (Origin AWS_KMS or EXTERNAL/CloudHSM custom key store), not embedded with the data (secure).
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Architecture review confirming keys are not recoverable from a stolen disk/snapshot alone.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Architecture review confirms at-rest encryption keys live in a separate trust domain from the storage they protect; keys are not recoverable from a stolen disk/snapshot alone.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-209 Security Guidelines for Storage Infrastructure

option_description: Whether a key-encryption-key wraps per-object data-encryption keys (envelope encryption), so DEKs are never stored or used in plaintext.
security_impact: Satisfies "Keys held in a dedicated KMS/HSM with envelope encryption" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when envelope_encryption_kek_dek_split is true alongside keys_managed_in_hsm_or_kms. Ensures a leaked persisted DEK is useless without the KMS-held KEK (ATT&CK T1552, M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Generate a data key from the KEK to demonstrate the envelope pattern in use.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Returns Plaintext (used locally to encrypt, then discarded) and CiphertextBlob (the wrapped DEK persisted alongside data) — demonstrating the KEK/DEK envelope pattern.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Design review confirming DEKs are wrapped by a KMS KEK and stored separately from data, with KEKs separate from DEKs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Design review confirms DEKs are generated/wrapped by a KMS KEK (e.g. KMS GenerateDataKey returns plaintext + ciphertext DEK; only the ciphertext DEK is persisted). DEKs stored separately from data, and KEKs stored separately from DEKs.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 Recommendation for Key Management

option_description: Whether the KMS/key policy has automatic rotation enabled for the keys protecting this data, rather than using a key indefinitely.
security_impact: Satisfies "Key rotation on a bounded cryptoperiod" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when key_rotation_enabled is true together with key_rotation_period_days <= 365. Bounds the cryptoperiod per NIST SP 800-57 (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query whether automatic key rotation is enabled for the key.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: KeyRotationEnabled: true (secure). false = key never rotated. Mirrors CIS AWS KMS.4.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS — Rotate AWS KMS keys (developer guide)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a documented rotation schedule exists per key type.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented cryptoperiod per key type with a defined rotation schedule; NIST 800-57 assigns bounded cryptoperiods rather than indefinite use.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 Recommendation for Key Management

option_description: The configured key cryptoperiod in days; <= 365 satisfies NIST SP 800-57 bounded-cryptoperiod guidance.
security_impact: Satisfies "Key rotation on a bounded cryptoperiod" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when key_rotation_period_days <= 365 together with key_rotation_enabled true. Keeps the originator-usage period bounded so a compromised key has limited reach (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured rotation interval; the KMS default is 365 days and is configurable via RotationPeriodInDays.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: KeyRotationEnabled: true with RotationPeriodInDays bounded (default 365). A value <= 365 satisfies the rule; rotation off or unbounded is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS — Rotate AWS KMS keys (developer guide)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the documented cryptoperiod per key type matches NIST 800-57 originator-usage guidance.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented cryptoperiod per key type (e.g. ~1-2 yr originator-usage for symmetric data-encryption keys) rather than indefinite use.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 Recommendation for Key Management

option_description: Whether the key policy/grants are scoped to specific principals and actions with no kms:* wildcard, following least privilege.
security_impact: Satisfies "Least-privilege key policy with separation of duties" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when kms_key_protection_policy_enforced is true together with kms_admin_separated_from_db_admin. Removes the over-broad grant that lets a principal both administer and decrypt with the key (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve the key policy and check for any kms:* wildcard grant to a broad principal.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No statement granting Action 'kms:*' to a broad principal (secure). A kms:* grant gives a principal both administer AND use of the key.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm IAM policies referencing the key are likewise scoped and contain no kms:* wildcard.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IAM policies grant only the specific KMS actions a principal needs; no kms:* in IAM or key policy.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

option_description: Whether separation of duties holds: principals that administer keys are distinct from those that administer or read the data store.
security_impact: Satisfies "Least-privilege key policy with separation of duties" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when kms_admin_separated_from_db_admin is true together with kms_key_protection_policy_enforced. Prevents a single custodian from both accessing data and exporting keys (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the key policy to confirm admin roles cannot use the key and user roles cannot administer it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key policy review: administrator roles that create/delete keys do NOT hold kms:Decrypt/kms:Encrypt; services that use the key do NOT hold administrative actions. Some services need only Encrypt, not Decrypt.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm storage-infra duties separate key management from data access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Storage-infra review confirms key-management duties are separated from data-access duties so a single custodian cannot both access data and export keys.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-209 Security Guidelines for Storage Infrastructure

option_description: Whether encryption uses org-controlled customer-managed/BYOK keys rather than provider-default keys, enabling independent rotation, policy, and revocation.
security_impact: Satisfies "Customer-managed keys with crypto-shred deletion" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when customer_managed_key_used is true together with secure_deletion_or_crypto_shred. Gives the org policy control needed for independent revocation and crypto-shred (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether the key is customer-managed or provider-managed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CUSTOMER (org-controlled, secure) vs AWS (provider-managed, less control). Customer-managed keys are preferred for granular access/rotation/deletion control.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the org holds the key policy and can enable/disable, rotate, and schedule deletion of the key.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Org controls the key policy with rights to enable/disable, rotate, and schedule deletion — not a provider-default key the org cannot govern.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether a documented secure-deletion path exists whereby destroying the key (crypto-shred) renders the data irrecoverable.
security_impact: Satisfies "Customer-managed keys with crypto-shred deletion" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when secure_deletion_or_crypto_shred is true together with customer_managed_key_used. Enables NIST Purge-level cryptographic erase for secure deletion and data-residency exit (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a working key-deletion (crypto-shred) path by scheduling deletion of a test key.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key scheduled for deletion; once deleted, all data encrypted under it is permanently unrecoverable (cryptographic erase). Confirms a working crypto-shred path.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the sanitization procedure maps key destruction to NIST 800-88 Purge-level cryptographic erase.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Sanitization procedure maps key destruction to NIST 800-88 Purge-level cryptographic erase for the media's confidentiality impact.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 Guidelines for Media Sanitization

option_description: Whether KMS API calls and key-administration events are captured to a tamper-evident audit trail (e.g. CloudTrail/KMS logs).
security_impact: Satisfies "Key-usage and key-management audit logging" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when key_management_audit_logging_enabled is true together with secret_access_audited. Makes misuse of decrypt/admin rights visible for accountability (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Look up KMS events in CloudTrail to confirm key-usage and key-admin operations are logged.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: KMS Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/RotateKey/ScheduleKeyDeletion events present with source IP and principal (secure); absent = key use is unaudited.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the trail is tamper-evident (e.g. log file validation / immutable retention) so key-admin events cannot be silently altered.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Audit trail has integrity protection (log-file validation or immutable/WORM retention) and is not writable by the key administrators it records.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether each key/secret access is logged with the requesting principal and source IP, enabling forensic attribution.
security_impact: Satisfies "Key-usage and key-management audit logging" — one of that countermeasure's AND-conditions — firing when secret_access_audited is true together with key_management_audit_logging_enabled. Provides per-access attribution so abuse of granted decrypt rights is traceable (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect KMS access events in CloudTrail and confirm each carries the principal identity and source IP.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: KMS Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey events present, each recording userIdentity (principal) and sourceIPAddress; absent or anonymized = inadequate attribution.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS KMS encryption best practices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For a non-AWS secrets store, confirm access logs capture principal and source IP per read.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secrets/KMS access log records the requesting principal and source IP on every key/secret retrieval.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge
